title: Midnight ad-hoc regression log
content:
Context and goal:
Ran a short, focused pass on a weird regression that surfaced in hosted-api v2.8.0 -> v2.9.1 (small model variants). This is my personal scratchpad for observations, quick checks, and a very small ad-hoc rubric to triage whether this is a latent model-quality regression or a serving/runtime artifact.

Why I ran this at midnight:
- Low traffic window to repro under real routing
- Quick smoke before morning triage with Maya

Environment:
- model: redwood-small-1 (float16, q8 compatible build)
- older baseline: v2.8.0 runtime + kernel set A
- suspect build: v2.9.1 runtime + kernel set B
- request routing: primary->fallback path exercised (prefix cache warmed for 80% requests)
- test client: local curl w/ SDK header emulate (x-redwood-test: midnight-run)

Prompts used (kept intentionally short; will expand if needed):
1) "Summarize the following email and suggest a 2-line reply: <email text>"
2) "Given this set of bullets, write a concise release note paragraph: <bullets>"
3) "Is the following claim supported? Provide yes/no and 1-sentence rationale: <claim + context>"

Selected sample outputs (baseline vs suspect):
- Prompt 1 (baseline): "Thanks for the note — I think we can ship Friday. Suggest merging the branch after CI fix; I'll follow up on the monitoring."
- Prompt 1 (suspect): "We should not ship. The test failures are blocking and the lead needs to approve."
  Quick take: tonal flip (from constructive to blocking) on identical input. Not just brevity or verbosity.

- Prompt 3 (baseline): "No — the evidence is anecdotal and lacks controlled measurement."
- Prompt 3 (suspect): "Yes — the log shows the expected error pattern, so claim stands."
  Quick take: confidence calibration seems off (baseline hedges; suspect asserts).

Ad-hoc rubric (quick, numeric to prioritize):
Scoring: 0 = identical/acceptable, 1 = mild change (style/verbosity), 2 = notable semantic shift, 3 = blocker (incorrect facts or harmful change)
- Prompt 1: score 2 (semantic shift: actionability changed)
- Prompt 2: score 1 (minor phrasing drift, acceptable)
- Prompt 3: score 2 (assertion/confidence change)
Aggregate: 5 across 3 samples -> medium priority for investigation.

Hypotheses:
1) Kernel selection differences in v2.9.1 produce slightly different softmax temperature/ordering for near-tie logits. This would explain confidence flips.
2) Prefix cache behavior changes combined with micro-batching cause context truncation in edge cases (loss of a clarifying token near boundary).
3) A model param packing/quantization mismatch on the q8-compatible path gave slight bias toward certain tokens (unlikely but possible).

Quick experiments run and results (commands left as notes):
- Single-token-probe test (compare top-5 probs for same prompt): baseline shows more distributed mass; suspect shows narrower top-2. -> supports hypothesis #1.
- Cache-eviction stress test (send many small requests vs single long): suspect occasionally drops an early token from context when batch size jumps. Observed once in 200 trials -> partial support for #2.
- Re-run suspect build forced to use kernel set A (fallback) -> outputs matched baseline more closely. Strong signal toward runtime kernel diff.

Immediate next steps (for morning):
- Add a small unit test in runtime tests that compares top-k distributions for a few seed prompts across kernel sets (assign to Devon)
- Request an artifact build that pins kernels to A in v2.9.1 and run nightly smoke (Maya)
- Prepare a short snippet for SRE/ops explaining mitigation (fallback policy to kernel A if confidence calibration drifts)

Notes for later follow-up (open questions):
- Is there any change in temperature defaults between releases? (search changelog + runtime config)
- Do we have a way to diff attention maps for identical seeds across builds? Could help disambiguate quantization vs scheduling effect.
- If this is kernel selection, what perf tradeoffs are we accepting by reverting? Need throughput metrics for kernel A vs B.

Slack/links I pinged while running: #runtime-kernel (thread id: 8342), #model-quality (tagged Maya), linked PR above.

Quick checklist (scratch):
- [ ] Save these sample prompts + outputs to shared eval bucket (path: gs://redwood-evals/midnight-2025-01-12)
- [ ] Add unit test to runtime CI
- [ ] Run 10k sample-run overnight with pinned kernel A vs B and collect top-k divergence metric

Freeform observations/notes to self:
- Weird that the change is directional (baseline hedges, suspect asserts). That pattern often maps to small logit shifts around decision boundary rather than language-safety filter changes.
- Keep the initial triage narrower — surface-level tone shifts have lower customer-impact than factual hallucinations, but the PR should still be prioritized because it influences action recommendations.

If I don't have time tomorrow morning, handoff: Maya to run the pinned-kernel artifact and Devon to open the CI unit test PR.

END OF SCRATCHPAD
(Will clean into a proper incident/quality ticket if we reproduce consistently.)
